name: Knuckle Pads-Leukonychia-Sensorineural Deafness-Palmoplantar Hyperkeratosis Syndrome
aliases: Knuckle Pads with Leukonychia and Deafness Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, thickened fibrotic nodules over the dorsal aspects of the interphalangeal joints (knuckle pads)
Congenital or early-onset leukonychia characterized by white discoloration of the nail plates
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Diffuse or focal thickening of the skin on palms and soles

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of knuckle pads, leukonychia, and sensorineural deafness
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by audiometric and dermatological evaluation; genetic testing may confirm diagnosis if available.

searchTerms: combined sensorineural and conductive hearing loss

laboratory: Audiometric confirmation of sensorineural hearing loss
imaging: MRI of inner ear may show cochlear nerve hypoplasia (rarely performed)
other: Histopathology of knuckle pads shows fibrosis and hyperkeratosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of knuckle pads and leukonychia but with palmoplantar keratoderma and deafness due to GJB2 mutations
Sensorineural deafness but absence of leukonychia

redFlags: Progressive sensorineural hearing loss leading to profound deafness
Rapid worsening of palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with fissuring
Development of joint contractures or severe finger stiffness
